title: Siblings and Cousins
blurb: Family secrets, childhood crimes and who got away with what. Best played with relatives.

truth: What's the worst thing you did to a sibling or cousin as a kid?
Who was the favourite in your family, and does everyone know it?
What's the best prank you ever pulled at home?
What's your funniest memory of a family holiday?
What's something you blamed on a sibling or cousin that was actually you?
Who in the family would survive longest in a zombie apocalypse?
What's the worst nickname your family gave you?
What's a toy you fought over with a sibling or cousin?
Who in your family has the loudest laugh?
What's a family tradition you secretly love?
What's the most embarrassing family photo of you?
Which relative would make the best prime minister?
What's your funniest memory at a family wedding or funeral?
What's the most unexpected thing a grandparent has taught you?
What did your family always argue about at the dinner table?
What's the worst thing you've ever been grounded for?
What's the best thing you've ever received from a relative?
Which relative do you get compared to most often?
What's the best hiding spot you ever found in your childhood home?
What's a family recipe that nobody should ever try to recreate?
What would your sibling or cousin say is your most annoying habit?
What's the worst haircut a family member ever gave you?
dare: Do your best impression of your mum, dad or auntie telling everyone off.
Act out your sibling or cousin losing at a board game.
Do an impression of Grandma or Grandpa trying to use a smartphone.
Perform the 'family photo' pose everyone does badly at Christmas.
Give a heartfelt apology to the sibling or cousin you wronged the most, in character.
Pretend to be a parent searching for the TV remote for the fifth time.
Narrate the sibling next to you eating, like a nature documentary.
Challenge a willing player to a best-of-three thumb war.
Pull a face like one of your relatives and have the group guess who it is.
Hide a small object in the room and see who finds it first.
Mime a classic backyard game you played as kids, and let the others guess it.
Tell a bedtime story in 20 seconds using only silly voices.
Make up a chant to settle who gets the front seat, and lead it.
Show the group how you used to dance when you were five.
Give a toast to the relative who always makes the best desserts.
Act out getting caught sneaking a biscuit before dinner.
Do a dramatic reading of an imaginary note sent home from school.
Mimic the way your sibling or cousin laughs.
Do an impression of the way your funniest relative walks.
Re-enact a classic family car argument over the radio station.
Play the part of the youngest in the family trying to be taken seriously.
Pretend to be a family reporter announcing the family news, whether true or silly.
Teach the group a childhood hand-clap game, or invent one on the spot.
